title: Multi-tenant scopes and object-level permission
outcome: Keep workspace identity in reads, writes, caches, jobs, and tests.
useCase: B2B workspaces and delayed background actions.
benefits: Protects cross-tenant data and makes scope testable.
drawbacks: Implicit context is convenient but easy to lose across jobs and caches.
cue: Carry the scope through every boundary.

trace.title: Trusted workspace
trace.detail: Authentication answers who the caller is. A tenant/workspace scope answers which records belong to the current context. Authorization answers which actions are allowed on those records. None replaces the others.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Follow the workspace from trusted membership lookup through the record query, policy, service, and result. Repeat the trace for a worker and cached read. Name where revocation takes effect.

Create two synthetic workspaces with colliding local identifiers and users with different roles. Test direct requests and jobs, not only hidden UI buttons.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: A global find followed by a client-supplied workspace ID can authorize the wrong row. Reusing an unscoped cached object can bypass the intended query boundary.
